newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Esso Sekiyu profits fell 18 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Japan Esso Sekiyu profits fell 18 pct in 1996.

text.p: Esso Sekiyu K.K., an affiliate of U.S. oil major Exxon Corp said on Friday its current profits in 1996 fell by 18 percent from the previous year, marking a decline for the second consecutive year.
The oil product wholesaler's current profits in 1996 amounted to 10.5 billion yen, down 2.3 billion yen from 12.8 billion yen in 1995.
Esso Sekiyu blamed the fall on domestic oil product retail prices remaining poor and failing to track a sharp rise in crude procurement costs.

"The yen-based priced of imported crude rose by about 30 percent in 1996 from the previous year due to surging crude prices combined with the weaker yen against the dollar," Nobuaki Miyajima, managing director of Esso Sekiyu, said.
"The retail price of gasoline continued to fall after Japan's oil product import market was liberalised at the end of last March," Miyajima said.
Esso Sekiyu's sales of oil products in 1996 increased by four percent from a year earlier to 11.5 million kilolitres, Miyajima said.
Current profit is pretax and includes gains or losses on non-operating activities, such as investment in stocks.
